subject: general
question: Which Amendment of the Indian Constitution added Article 39A (free legal aid)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment** of the Indian Constitution, enacted in 1976 during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, is one of the most comprehensive amendments in India's constitutional history.
 
• It introduced Article 39A to the Directive Principles of State Policy, which mandates the state to ensure that the legal system promotes justice on the basis of equal opportunity and provides free legal aid to economically weaker sections.
 
• This amendment is often referred to as the **"Mini Constitution"** due to its extensive impact on various parts of the Constitution.
 
• Article 39A emphasizes the importance of equal justice and free legal aid and aims to reduce the inequality of access to justice caused by economic or other disabilities.
 
• It highlights the responsibility of the state to ensure justice for all, irrespective of financial or social status, and aligns with the constitutional goal of securing social, economic, and political justice for citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **86th Amendment (2002)**

 
 
• The 86th Amendment added Article 21A to the Constitution, making the right to education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It also modified Article 45, requiring the state to provide early childhood care and education for children below 6 years.
 
• This amendment ensures free and compulsory education for all children in the specified age group.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment (1978)**
 
 
• The 44th Amendment was enacted to revoke many provisions of the 42nd Amendment and restore the original spirit of the Constitution.
 
• It removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This amendment also strengthened civil liberties and restored judicial independence.
 
 
 
• **73rd Amendment (1992)**
 
 
• The 73rd Amendment introduced the Panchayati Raj system in India, giving constitutional status to rural local self-government.
 
• It added Part IX (The Panchayats) and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, listing 29 subjects under Panchayat jurisdiction.
 
• This amendment provided for a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and ensured regular elections and reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women.
